literal: he won over the old territory and the distant and near submitted.
idiomatic: he won back the old territory until distant and near submitted.

literal: When Zong surrendered, Yanming pressed on with the army.
idiomatic: When Zong surrendered, Yanming pressed the army forward.

literal: He recovered the southeastern borderlands, reaching Su and Yu, then returned.
idiomatic: He recovered the southeast to Su and Yu, then returned.

literal: He was promoted Commander and Governor of Xu Province.
idiomatic: He was made Commander and Governor of Xu Province.

literal: Repeated campaigns had worn the land and people.
idiomatic: Repeated campaigns had ravaged land and people.

literal: Yanming won over old and new inhabitants until all were settled and the people attached.
idiomatic: Yanming won over old and new until all were settled and the people attached.

literal: Under Emperor Zhuang he also held Grand Marshal.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhuang he also held Grand Marshal.

literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Yanming received Hao's trust.
idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Yanming received his trust.

literal: When Hao was defeated he fled to Liang and died south of the Yangtze.
idiomatic: When Hao was defeated he fled to Liang and died south of the Yangtze.

literal: At the end of Emperor Zhuang's reign his coffin was returned.
idiomatic: At the end of Zhuang's reign his coffin returned.

literal: At the start of Xiaowu he was posthumously made Grand Guardian, princely title as before, posthumous name Wensuan.
idiomatic: At Xiaowu's accession he was posthumously Grand Guardian with princely title unchanged and name Wensuan.

literal: Works composed: more than three hundred pieces of poetry, fu, encomia, hymns, inscriptions, and dirges.
idiomatic: He composed more than three hundred poems, fu, encomia, hymns, inscriptions, and dirges.

literal: He also compiled Overview of the Five Classics and Separate Meanings of the Odes and Rites;
idiomatic: He also compiled Overview of the Five Classics and Separate Meanings of the Odes and Rites;

literal: annotated Records of Emperors and Kings and Lives of Immortals.
idiomatic: annotated Records of Emperors and Kings and Lives of Immortals.

literal: He also took Xin Dufang of Hejian, skilled in calculation and diagrams.
idiomatic: He also employed Xin Dufang of Hejian, skilled in calculation and diagrams.

literal: He gathered nine chapters of Standards of Implements; Fang wrote a separate commentary—both circulated in the age.
idiomatic: He gathered nine chapters of Standards of Implements with Fang's commentary—both circulated.

literal: His grandson Changru, under Emperor Xiaojing, inherited his grandfather's title.
idiomatic: His grandson Changru inherited under Emperor Xiaojing.

literal: Emperor Xianwen had seven sons: the Reflective Empress bore Emperor Xiaowen;
idiomatic: Xianwen had seven sons: the Reflective Empress bore Xiaowen;

literal: Consort Feng the Worthy bore the Prince of Xianyang Xi;
idiomatic: Consort Feng the Worthy bore the Prince of Xianyang, Xi;

literal: Consort Han the Worthy bore the Prince of Zhao Commandery the Spiritual Gan and the Prince of Gaoyang the Cultivated and Solemn Yong;
idiomatic: Consort Han bore the Prince of Zhao Commandery the Spiritual Gan and the Prince of Gaoyang the Cultivated Yong;

literal: Consort Meng of the Pepper Chambers bore the Prince of Guangling the Sagacious Yu;
idiomatic: Consort Meng bore the Prince of Guangling the Sagacious Yu;

literal: Consort Pan the Worthy bore the Prince of Pengcheng the Martial and Proclaimed Xie;
idiomatic: Consort Pan bore the Prince of Pengcheng the Martial Xie;

literal: Consort Gao of the Pepper Chambers bore the Prince of Beihai Xiang.
idiomatic: Consort Gao bore the Prince of Beihai Xiang.

literal: Prince of Xianyang Xi, styled Siyong, was enfeoffed in the ninth year of Taihe and made Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Director of the Palace at the Center.
idiomatic: The Prince of Xianyang, Xi, styled Siyong, was enfeoffed in the ninth year of Taihe and made Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Director of the Palace at the Center.

literal: Empress Dowager Wenming ordered imperial sons and grandsons to a separate school at Jing's place, choosing loyal, trustworthy, and broadly learned men as teachers to shape them.
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming placed imperial sons in a separate school, choosing loyal and learned teachers to shape them.

literal: Xiaowen, because the princes held the three capital judiciaries, told Xi: "You are all young yet bear heavy duty; the three capitals' judging of cases especially demands care.
idiomatic: Xiaowen told Xi and the others: "You are young yet bear heavy duty; judging in the three capitals especially demands care.

literal: To hand one a knife who cannot wield it and bid him cut brocade is not the brocade's chief fault but the fault of him who gave the knife.
idiomatic: Giving a knife to one who cannot wield it and bidding him cut brocade faults not the brocade but the giver.

literal: Empress Dowager Wenming also sent admonitions and encouragement.
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming also sent admonitions.

literal: Sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Opener of the Office, and Governor of Ji Province; Xiaowen feasted him at the southern suburb.
idiomatic: He went out as Bearer of the Staff, Opener of the Office, and Governor of Ji; Xiaowen feasted him at the southern suburb.

literal: He also sent word of the affair of the Prince of Jiyang Yu, wrongly executed by law, to admonish Xi.
idiomatic: He reported the wrongful execution of the Prince of Jiyang Yu as further admonition.

literal: Later when Xi came to the capital, an edict made Director of the Court Li Chong Xi's teacher.
idiomatic: When Xi came to court, Li Chong was made his teacher.

literal: At the time a prince's household aide should be taken from the eight clans and families of pure conduct; Xi took retainers of the Prince of Rencheng—deeply rebuked by the emperor.
idiomatic: A prince's aides should come from the eight clans; Xi took the Prince of Rencheng's retainers and was deeply rebuked.

literal: Because the princes' marriages were mostly base, he betrothed Xi to the daughter of former Governor of Yingchuan Longxi Li Fu;
idiomatic: Because princely marriages were base, Xi was betrothed to Li Fu's daughter of Yingchuan;

literal: the Prince of Henan Gan to the daughter of former Central Scribe of Dai Commandery Mu Mingle;
idiomatic: the Prince of Henan Gan to Mu Mingle's daughter;

literal: the Prince of Guangling Yu to the daughter of Staff Officer of Agile Cavalry Rongyang Zheng Pingcheng;
idiomatic: the Prince of Guangling Yu to Zheng Pingcheng's daughter;

literal: the Prince of Yingchuan Yong to the daughter of former Doctor of the Secretariat Luyang Lu Shenbao;
idiomatic: the Prince of Yingchuan Yong to Lu Shenbao's daughter;

literal: the Prince of Shiping Xie to the daughter of Director of the Court Longxi Li Chong;
idiomatic: the Prince of Shiping Xie to Li Chong's daughter;

literal: the Prince of Beihai Xiang to the daughter of Bureau Director Rongyang Zheng Yi.
idiomatic: the Prince of Beihai Xiang to Zheng Yi's daughter.

literal: The authorities memorialized: "Three thousand men of Ji Province, led by Su Senguan, call Xi clear and bright with benevolent government, and ask hereditary fief in Ji Province.
idiomatic: Authorities reported: "Three thousand men of Ji, led by Su Senguan, praise Xi's clarity and benevolence and ask hereditary fief in Ji."

literal: An edict said: "Territory is drawn by the ruler; principle does not allow petition from below.
idiomatic: An edict said: "Territory is the ruler's to draw; subjects may not petition from below."

literal: He entered office as Governor of Si Province.
idiomatic: He became Governor of Si Province.

literal: An edict, because Xi was the eldest younger brother, gave him three thousand households; the other five princes each two thousand.
idiomatic: Because Xi was the eldest younger brother he received three thousand households; the other five princes two thousand each.

literal: Xiaowen received the court ministers and ordered an end to northern speech, all following standard pronunciation; Xi praised and completed the matter.
idiomatic: Xiaowen ordered court to abandon northern speech for standard pronunciation; Xi praised the policy.

literal: Then an edict: "Those thirty and above, long accustomed, perhaps cannot be suddenly changed.
idiomatic: An edict followed: "Those thirty and above, long accustomed, perhaps cannot change at once.

literal: Those thirty and below now in court—speech must not remain as before.
idiomatic: Those thirty and below in court must not keep old speech.

literal: Whoever deliberately persists shall be lowered in rank and dismissed from office.
idiomatic: Deliberate persistence means lowered rank and dismissal.

literal: If old custom remains, I fear that after several generations below Yi and Luo they will again become people with loose hair.
idiomatic: If custom remains, after generations below Yi and Luo they may again become loose-haired barbarians."

literal: I once discussed this with Li Chong; Chong said: "Of the speech of the four quarters, who knows which is right?
idiomatic: I once discussed this with Li Chong, who said, "Of the speech of the four quarters, who knows which is right?

literal: What the emperor speaks is then orthodox—why must one change the old and follow the new?
idiomatic: What the emperor speaks is orthodox—why change the old for the new?"

literal: Chong's words deserve death in principle.
idiomatic: Chong's words deserved death in principle."

literal: He then told Chong: "You have truly failed the altars of soil and grain.
idiomatic: He told Chong: "You have failed the altars of soil and grain."

literal: Chong removed his cap and apologized.
idiomatic: Chong removed his cap and apologized.

literal: He also rebuked officials who remained in the capital: "Yesterday I saw women's dress still with overlapping collars and narrow sleeves—why violate the former edict?
idiomatic: He rebuked capital officials: "Yesterday I saw women still in overlapping collars and narrow sleeves—why violate the edict?"

literal: Xi replied: "Your Majesty's sagacity surpasses Yao and Shun, transforming the central plains.
idiomatic: Xi replied: "Your Majesty surpasses Yao and Shun, transforming the central plains.

literal: The crime of violation truly deserves punishment.
idiomatic: Violation deserves punishment."

literal: Xiaowen said: "If Our words are wrong, you should debate boldly in court—why in enter flatter the intent and in withdraw not follow?
idiomatic: Xiaowen said: "If We err, debate in court—why flatter Us in session and disobey in private?

literal: In antiquity Shun told Yu: 'Do not agree to my face and afterward speak behind my back.'
idiomatic: Shun told Yu: Do not agree to my face and speak behind my back—is this not you?"

literal: Is this not what you are!"
idiomatic: Is this not what you mean!"

literal: Soon Xi was made concurrent Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: Soon Xi was made concurrent Grand Commandant.

literal: Later the emperor visited Xi's residence and told Minister of Works Mu Liang and Vice Director Li Chong: "Younger brother Xi is kin to the imperial pole and long holds concurrent Grand Commandant to harmonize the cauldron; We always fear the ruler has the name of empty appointment and ministers the wound of failing each other.
idiomatic: Visiting Xi's home, the emperor told Mu Liang and Li Chong: "Xi is imperial kin and long concurrent Grand Commandant; We fear empty titles for the ruler and mutual failure for ministers.

literal: Now visiting his house, We have only wronged you two guests—truly ashamed.
idiomatic: Today We wrong only you two guests—truly ashamed."

literal: The emperor was deep in brotherly feeling; because Xi was next eldest he treated him with exceptional courtesy.
idiomatic: Deep in brotherly feeling, he treated Xi, next eldest, with exceptional courtesy.

literal: Yet he also knew his greedy nature and often admonished him sharply, but in the end he did not change his conduct.
idiomatic: Yet knowing his greed he often admonished him, without changing his conduct.

literal: Later he was made Palace Attendant and regular Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: He was later made Palace Attendant and regular Grand Commandant.

literal: When the emperor died, Xi received the testamentary regency.
idiomatic: At the emperor's death Xi received testamentary regency.

literal: Though head among the regents, he secretly received bribes.
idiomatic: Though head regent, he secretly took bribes.

literal: He had several dozen concubines and was not yet satisfied, still wishing to choose from afar to indulge his desires.
idiomatic: He had dozens of concubines and still wished to choose more from afar.

literal: Xuanwu greatly disliked this.
idiomatic: Xuanwu greatly disliked this.

literal: In spring of the second year of Jingming he summoned Xi and others to Guangji Hall and said: "Ke is lately ill and truly relies on his uncles.
idiomatic: In spring of Jingming's second year he summoned them to Guangji Hall: "Ke is ill and relies on his uncles.

literal: Now he will personally hold the hundred offices.
idiomatic: Now he will personally govern.

literal: Return to your princely offices; separate disposition will follow.
idiomatic: Return to your offices; We will dispose separately."

literal: Soon an edict advanced him to Grand Guardian and head Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: Soon he was advanced to Grand Guardian and head Grand Commandant.

literal: When the emperor took government, Xi was uneasy and with his consort's brother, Concurrent Attendant of the Yellow Gate Li Boshang, plotted rebellion.
idiomatic: When the emperor took power Xi was uneasy and with Li Boshang, his consort's brother, plotted rebellion.

literal: The emperor was then at Xiaoping; Xi was at a small residence west of the city.
idiomatic: The emperor was at Xiaoping; Xi at a small residence west of the city.

literal: At first he wished to lead troops straight into Jincheng; the host was disheartened and divided.
idiomatic: He meant to lead troops into Jincheng; the host wavered and split.

literal: Xi's heart slackened; from dawn to dusk he could not decide.
idiomatic: His heart slackened; from dawn to dusk he could not decide.

literal: They agreed to disperse without leaking the plot.
idiomatic: They agreed to disperse without revealing the plot.

literal: Duty Attendants Fu Chengzu and Xue Weisun with Xi were to harm the emperor.
idiomatic: Duty attendants Fu Chengzu and Xue Weisun were to kill the emperor with Xi.

literal: That day the emperor rested on Mang Mountain below the shadow of a pagoda; after a little he slept; Weisun wished to rush the hall.
idiomatic: That day the emperor rested on Mang Mountain beneath a pagoda; Weisun meant to rush the hall.

literal: Chengzu privately told Weisun: "I hear that whoever kills the Son of Heaven his body will break out in sores.
idiomatic: Chengzu whispered: "Whoever kills the Son of Heaven breaks out in sores."

literal: Weisun for the moment stopped.
idiomatic: Weisun stopped.

literal: The emperor soon awoke.
idiomatic: The emperor soon awoke.

literal: Presently Prince of Wuxing Yang Jishi came out and at once rode to report.
idiomatic: Prince of Wuxing Yang Jishi came out and rode to report.

literal: Xi still did not suspect; he went with concubines toward Hongchi Villa and sent his fast officer Liu Xiaogou with a memorial saying he was inspecting fields and herds.
idiomatic: Xi, still unsuspecting, went with concubines to Hongchi Villa and sent Liu Xiaogou with a memorial claiming to inspect fields.

literal: Xiaogou reached Mang Ridge and already met soldiers; they wondered at Xiaogou's red dress and were about to kill him.
idiomatic: Xiaogou met soldiers on Mang Ridge; they wondered at his red dress and nearly killed him.

literal: Xiaogou said he wished to report rebellion, and they spared him.
idiomatic: He said he came to report rebellion and was spared.

literal: That night Xi lodged at Hongchi, not knowing the affair was exposed.
idiomatic: That night Xi lodged at Hongchi, unaware the plot was exposed.

literal: That night soldiers everywhere pursued Xi; Xi fled southeast from Hongchi; of those who followed Xi only Concurrent Guard Yin Longwu.
idiomatic: Soldiers pursued him; he fled southeast from Hongchi with only Yin Longwu.

literal: Xi in distress said: "Try to make a riddle; I shall think to solve it and ease this bitter vexation.
idiomatic: In distress Xi said: "Make a riddle—I will solve it to ease this torment."

literal: Longwu suddenly recalled an old riddle: "Sleeping we sleep together, rising we rise together, greedy as jackals and wolves, yet booty does not enter oneself.
idiomatic: Longwu recalled: "Sleeping we sleep together, rising we rise together, greedy as jackals and wolves, yet booty never enters oneself."

literal: He had no thought of plotting assassination.
idiomatic: He had no thought of assassination.

literal: Xi also did not take it as satire of himself and solved: "This is the eye.
idiomatic: Xi did not take it as satire and said: "The eye."

literal: But Longwu meant chopsticks.
idiomatic: Longwu meant chopsticks.

literal: Crossing the Luo, at Baiwu he turned to Longwu: "You should steel your heart and make the plan to die with the Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: At Baiwu he said: "Steel your heart and die with the Grand Commandant."

literal: Longwu said: "If I share fate with Your Highness, though I die I yet live.
idiomatic: Longwu said: "To share Your Highness's fate is to live even in death."

literal: Soon Xi was seized and sent to Hualin Postal Pavilion; a thousand-jin lock was put on Longwu and armored guards watched them.
idiomatic: Soon Xi was seized at Hualin Postal Pavilion; Longwu was chained with a thousand-jin lock under armored guard.

literal: The heat was extreme; Xi thirsted and was near death; an order cut off water and drink.
idiomatic: In extreme heat Xi thirsted near death; orders cut off water.

literal: Palace Attendant Cui Guang ordered attendants to send more than a sheng of yogurt; Xi drank it in one draft.
idiomatic: Cui Guang sent more than a sheng of yogurt; Xi drank it at once.

literal: Earlier Xiaowen, observing the observatory, saw air of treasonous plotting and told Xi: "The stars change—you will end in treasonous plotting, accomplish nothing, and only receive evil.
idiomatic: Earlier Xiaowen saw treason in the stars and told Xi: "You will plot treason, accomplish nothing, and only suffer."

literal: At this it was indeed as he said.
idiomatic: Now it was as he said.
